transcription.tex: \textbf{1. STEP 2010 Q1}\par Given the identity\[5x^2+2y^2-6xy+4x-4y\equiv a(x-y+2)^2+b(cx+y)^2+d\]
Compare coefficients after expansion:\[a=1,\quad b=1,\quad c=-2,\quad d=-4\]
\textbf{2. MAT 2012 1G}\quad For which \(k\) do positive real \(x,y\) satisfy \(2x+ky=4\), \(x+y=k\)?\par A: all values; B: none; C: only 2; D: only \(k>-2\).
Substitute \(x=k-y\): \((k-2)(y+2)=0\). Since \(y>0\), we need \(k=2\). Positive pairs with \(x+y=2\) exist. Answer C.

transcription.tex: The graph of an equation contains all points \((x,y)\) satisfying it. For example, \((3,7)\) lies on \(y=2x+1\).
\textbf{Two simultaneous equations}\quad \[y=2x+1,\qquad x+y=5\]Which point satisfies both equations?
The point of intersection lies on both graphs.\[3x+1=5\Rightarrow(x,y)=(\tfrac43,\tfrac{11}3)\]

transcription.tex: On the same axes, draw \(y=3-2x\) and \(y=x^2-3x+1\).
\textbf{a. Intersections}\quad Use the graph to solve the simultaneous equations.
\textbf{b. Algebraic check}\quad How can we prove that there are two intersections?
\[x^2-3x+1=3-2x\Rightarrow x^2-x-2=0\]The discriminant is \(1+8=9>0\), so there are two distinct real solutions.

transcription.tex: Draw \(y=2x-2\) and \(y=x^2+4x+1\) on the same axes.
\textbf{Prove the graphs never meet}\quad Solve simultaneously and consider the discriminant.
\[\begin{aligned}x^2+4x+1&=2x-2\\x^2+2x+3&=0\\b^2-4ac&=4-12=-8<0\end{aligned}\]There are no real solutions and no intersections.

transcription.tex: The line \(y=2x+1\) meets \(kx^2+2y+(k-2)=0\) at exactly one point. The constant \(k\) is positive.
\[kx^2+2(2x+1)+k-2=0\Rightarrow kx^2+4x+k=0\]Exactly one real root requires\[16-4k^2=0\Rightarrow k=\pm2.\]Since \(k>0\), \(k=2\).

transcription.tex: \textbf{9.} A swimmer dives into a pool. Her vertical position \(p\) metres is modelled in terms of horizontal distance \(x\) metres from entry by\[p=\tfrac12x^2-3x.\]The pool bottom is modelled by \(p=0.3x-6\). Determine whether the swimmer touches the bottom.
\[\begin{aligned}0.5x^2-3x&=0.3x-6\\0.5x^2-3.3x+6&=0\\b^2-4ac&=10.89-12=-1.11<0\end{aligned}\]The graphs never intersect. The model predicts that she does not touch the pool bottom.

slides.title: Set Builder Notation

transcription.tex: A \textbf{set} is a collection of values. Order does not matter and there are no duplicates. Use braces, e.g. \(A=\{1,4,6,7\}\).
\(A\cap B\): intersection, elements in both sets.\par \(A\cup B\): union, elements in either set or both.\par \(\varnothing\): the empty set.
\(\mathbb N\): positive integers (our convention here).\par \(\mathbb Z\): all integers.\par \(\mathbb R\): all real numbers.\par \(x\in A\): x is a member of A.
